parakeet: Then God is not the conclusion of investigation. God is the starting assumption, smuggled in without scrutiny. And once we inspect that starting point, the virgin birth doesn't hold, the resurrection falls apart, the moral framework cracks, the promise of afterlife fizzle into fear-based marketing. The gods we're being asked to believe in don't exist in the evidence. They don't exist in experience. They only exist in the books that claim them, and only in those books. Remove the book and watch the God disappear. Because if Yahweh, Allah, or any other deity existed outside of Scripture, we wouldn't need preachers to defend them. They just exist. So I'm not trying to be edgy. I'm trying to be honest. And the honest truth is you cannot defend a being who doesn't exist without defending the book that made them up. And once that book fails the test, the God goes with it. I don't believe in your God, not because I'm mad at him, but because I finally had the courage to look for him outside the pages he was trapped in. And he wasn't there. Not a trace. Not a whisper, not even a footprint. Because belief in God isn't just unwarranted, it's non sequitur. There is no premise, no source, no signal, just a sacred echo bouncing inside a closed book.
